title: Circular Buffer
description: Fixed-capacity ring buffer — writes past capacity overwrite the oldest slot. Modular arithmetic on head/tail indices keeps it O(1) per op.

notes: Two indices (head=write, tail=read) plus a size counter — size disambiguates the full-vs-empty case where head === tail.
Decision: when full, additional writes overwrite the oldest element rather than throwing. Document the policy — both choices are valid.
All ops are O(1). Modulo on indices is the only trick — never reallocate.

questions.q: Why track `size` separately instead of inferring it from head and tail?
options: When head === tail, it could mean either full or empty — size resolves the ambiguity
It's a style preference, no functional reason

questions.q: On a write to a full buffer (overwrite policy), which pointer must advance besides head?
options: tail must also advance so the oldest entry is dropped

questions.q: Time complexity of read() and write() on a circular buffer?
After capacity=3 and writes [1,2,3,4,5], what does the next read() return?

exercises.prompt: Complete the wrap-around logic so reads return the oldest surviving values after overwrites.

blanks.hint: increment size when not yet full

L3.prompt: Implement CircularBuffer(capacity) with write(v), read(), and a `size` field. Writes past capacity overwrite the oldest. With cap=3: write 1,2,3,4 then log size, read, read, read, read.
hints: Modulo on head and tail is the only wrap-around logic you need.
When full, advance tail on each write so the oldest element is the one discarded.
Reading an empty buffer should return undefined, not throw.
